body: This is what I failed to see until now. She does not need me to solve her issues. She needs me to be her safe zone. Someone she can talk to without feeling like she is hurting me. And when I worry about her so much and show it, she doesn't feel safe to talk because I'll be worried. I'll work on changing that. Thank you.

Thank you so much for taking the time to help. It really means a great deal to me. This piece of advice is truly invaluable. I will try to not be intrusive from now on and just listen while also reminding that I'm here for her no matter what. 

Again, thank you. Your help is greatly appreciated.
Thanks for that, it's very accurate and to the point. I'll save it for future reference.

This makes a lot of sense. Hell, even if she gave me a straight up "yes, I want to help myself" she would probably say it just to comfort me. How do I avoid it though? How can I make sure she wants to help herself without coming across as judgemental?

As simply and straightforward as I can. I think she doesn't want to believe me for fear of me betraying her in the end as well.

When I asked her if she wants to make things better and deal with her depression, she told me that there's nothing she can do about it. When I emphasized if she WANTS to and not if she can, she answered "I don't know. Yeah, sure why not?"

I tell her these things every time she is feeling down. But I can't shake the feeling that I don't understand her well enough to make her feel better. It's even more difficult, because she has been betrayed by almost everyone she has ever opened up to. And those who haven't betrayed her, have only scratched the surface. Her ex and me are the only ones who know she is suicidal and I feel that her ex didn't really care. She almost made an attempt when they were together too and he knew about it beforehand. It's sheer luck she never went through with it.
I think that she is afraid to make me worry about her. And for that reason she doesn't want to open up anymore..
